text:
Connor Brown missed the start of the season and came back to a Devils team that wins almost every night. In nine games he has three goals and five points, two on the power play, and New Jersey has won eight of them.

Be careful with the scoring line. He has 1.53 expected goals and three actual goals, and 27.3 percent shooting is about double his usual range. The 5v5 picture is weaker: the Devils get 44 percent of the expected goals with him on, and 15.9 points worse relative to teammates, though nine games is a small sample.

His value is the stuff that doesn't show in points. A WDHA FM headline credited his return with a better penalty kill, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking flagged a signature: 19 percent of his setups go across the royal road, against 7 percent for a typical forward. Expect the goals to slow; the PK role and the passing should keep him in the lineup.
headline: Brown is back and finishing everything
